question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability at a Point
question.problem: Given $X∼\text{Geom}(0.15),$ compute $P(X=7).$  Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.15),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(0.85)}^{x-1}(0.15), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=7) & =f(7) \\  & ={(0.85)}^{6}(0.15) \\  & ≈0.0566.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Over a Bounded Interval Using the Complement
question.problem: Given $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{2}{3}),$ compute $P(X\ge 6)$ rounded to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{2}{3}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x-1}(\frac{2}{3}), & x=1,2,3… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X\ge 6.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & =1-P(X<6)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<6) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4,5\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5) \\  & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{0}(\frac{2}{3})+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{1}(\frac{2}{3})+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}(\frac{2}{3})+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{3}(\frac{2}{3})+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{4}(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & ≈0.9959.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & =1-P(X<6) \\  & ≈1-0.9959 \\  & =0.0041.\end{aligned}
$$
